title: Gavriel Iddan, an Israeli engineer from Rafael, invented a pill-sized camera that films the small intestine

trailer.text: Gavriel Iddan, an Israeli engineer who worked at Rafael, is the inventor of wireless capsule endoscopy.
His neighbor, the Israeli gastroenterologist Eitan Scapa, explained to him that the small bowel remained out of reach of medical examinations.
Iddan developed a pill-sized camera. The patient swallows it, and it sends signals to sensors worn on the body.
In 1998 Given Imaging was founded to market the invention, and Iddan was its chief technology officer in Yokneam.
According to the European Patent Office, capsule endoscopy became the global standard for small bowel diagnostics.

stations.title: Six meters that could not be seen

paragraphs.text: Gastroscopes and colonoscopes made it possible to examine the upper 1.2 meters and the lower 1.8 meters of the digestive tract.
But the middle 6 meters, the small intestine, remained more difficult to reach.
At times doctors were forced to use exploratory surgery to diagnose the small intestine.
This is a risky approach, and it is very uncomfortable for patients.
Gavriel Iddan was born in Haifa in 1941.
He is an electro-optical engineer and a graduate of the Technion.
In 1981 he took a sabbatical from his position as a senior engineer in the electro-optical design section of Rafael, the R&D branch of the Ministry of Defense.
His neighbor in Boston, Eitan Scapa, was an Israeli gastroenterologist who was also there on sabbatical.
Scapa explained to Iddan that fiber-optic technology left the small bowel out of reach of examinations.

According to ynet, after a meeting in 1998 with his neighbor, the gastroenterologist Prof. Eitan Scapa, Iddan began developing a pill with a video camera that would allow doctors to diagnose diseases and bleeding.
Iddan saw that missile technology could be miniaturized into a medical product.
According to Given's CEO, Gavriel Meron, Iddan realized he could make an ingestible "missile" that would transmit images.
In 1993 Iddan came up with an idea: to split the system into three parts.
In the mid-1990s he developed the idea of wireless capsule endoscopy.
He began the experiments with friends from Rafael and tested the idea on a frozen chicken he bought at the supermarket, he recounted.
There was an energy problem.
CCD elements consume a lot of energy, and miniature batteries were sufficient for 10 minutes of transmission at most.
Iddan came across an article by Eric Fossum in a journal on optical engineering.
CMOS chips consume only one percent of the energy of CCD elements.
In 1994 Iddan met Gavriel Meron, who raised the funds and recruited the physicists and engineers.
Dov Avni, who had worked at Rafael for many years, was given the task of creating a camera and a light source from scratch and miniaturizing all the components.
A leading expert at the Sarnoff Corporation predicted that it would be impossible to generate sharp images with CMOS technology.
Avni knew that engineers at Tower Semiconductor in Migdal Haemek had already solved the problem.
According to Discover, the capsule's camera was developed by Photobit, a California company.

stations.title: A company, a prototype and a first swallow

paragraphs.text: In 1997 two groups of researchers, in Israel and in London, joined forces to complete the development of the capsule.
That same year Meron met Paul Swain in Birmingham, and the two decided to work together.
In 1998 Given Imaging was founded to market the prototype.
Paul Swain, of the Royal London Hospital, was one of the developers of the capsule and a volunteer in the human trials.
According to a review in PMC, he was the first person in the world to swallow a capsule endoscope.
Scapa passed an endoscope into Swain without sedation and, with a snare, moved the capsule into the duodenum.
Ten healthy volunteers swallowed the capsules in the initial trial.
On 25 May 2000, Iddan, Meron, Glukhovsky and Swain published an article in Nature.
After publication, the capsule attracted widespread media coverage, which compared it to the miniaturised submarine in the film Fantastic Voyage.
The PillCam SB capsule measures 11 by 26 mm and weighs 3.7 grams.
Inside it are an imaging chip video camera, six LEDs, two silver-oxide batteries and a radio transmitter.
The patient swallows the capsule, and it travels safely through the digestive tract, as designed.
It sends signals to sensors worn on the body.
According to the European Patent Office, the data is transmitted at a rate of two images per second.
According to Discover, the capsule finally exits the body in the usual digestive way.
According to the European Patent Office, the patient can move around normally during the examination.
With PillCam SB, no sedation is needed.
According to Forward, at the end of the examination the doctor downloads the images from the receiver to a computer.
According to an old article in the Forward, each disposable camera then cost $450.
According to the same Forward article, doctors and hospitals then spent $17,500 on each workstation needed for the procedure and $5,450 on a recorder.
According to American gastroenterologists, the capsule revolutionized the diagnosis of small intestine disorders, which are difficult to see on X-rays or with more invasive methods.
Dr. Asher Kornbluth, a gastroenterologist in Manhattan, said the capsule makes it possible to see the interior of the small intestine with great clarity, not just shadows on an X-ray.
According to Meron, an analysis of data from 691 patients in 32 studies showed that the capsule helped doctors diagnose small intestine problems in about 60% of the patients.
According to Meron, all the other technologies combined found the source of the problem in only 40% of the patients.
According to Prof. Uri Kopylov of Sheba, the pill is more sensitive than MRI in detecting inflammatory findings in Crohn's disease.

According to Dr. Laurence Kesselbrenner, CEO of Medtronic Yokneam, in an ynet article published in collaboration with Medtronic, the PillCam for the colon saves lives, because without it many people would not undergo a colonoscopy.
The author of a review in PMC writes that Iddan told him about a doctor who told him that, thanks to the capsule, he was able to save a patient's life.
According to an ynet article published in collaboration with Medtronic, in 2001 the PillCam was approved for use in Israel and the United States, and later also in Europe.

According to the Forward, after the FDA approved the capsule in August 2001 as a secondary method only, in July of a later year it gave the company approval to sell it as a first-line test for small intestine problems.
According to Forward, the company planned to develop the capsule also for diagnosing problems in the stomach and the esophagus.
According to a Forward article written after 2001, as of June of the year of the article, about 600 hospitals and medical offices in the United States offered the test.
At that point some 32,000 Americans had already swallowed the capsule, along with another 20,000 in the rest of the world.
According to the European Patent Office, PillCam SB had been used close to 1.5 million times, by more than 5,000 medical facilities in more than 75 countries.
According to Jewish Link, more than two million capsule examinations are now performed worldwide each year.
On 8 December 2013 Covidien announced an agreement to acquire Given Imaging for $30 per share in cash.
According to an ynet article published in collaboration with Medtronic, the company was acquired several years later by Medtronic, which kept development and manufacturing in Israel.
According to an ynet article published in collaboration with Medtronic, the PillCam is a source of Israeli pride that millions of people around the world swallow today.
According to the European Patent Office, his camera opened up new possibilities in gastrointestinal diagnostics.
According to doctors, the device cannot treat the problems it finds.
The capsule has no surgical tools like a conventional endoscope for biopsies, treating bleeding or removing polyps.
Other researchers said that the capsule, at least in its form at the time, was too limited to replace endoscopes.
The main drawback of the PillCam and the capsules that followed it is the lack of control over their movement.
The relatively high cost of the disposable devices prevented them from overtaking conventional endoscopy.
Sometimes the capsule gets stuck at a stricture or an obstruction in the small intestine and has to be retrieved.

disagreements.question: How and when did Iddan meet Scapa?

versions.says: Review in PMC: in 1981, on sabbatical in Boston, when the two were neighbors
According to ynet, in 1998 Dr. Gabi Iddan met his neighbor, the gastroenterologist Prof. Eitan Scapa, who shared with him the difficulty of performing endoscopy in the small intestine.
Jewish Link: Iddan's neighbor fell ill with a stomach ailment, and then Iddan realized there was no technology for examining the small intestine

disagreements.question: What kind of engineer is Iddan?

versions.says: Forward: a mechanical engineer who worked on imaging devices at Rafael
Electro-optical engineer

European Patent Office: Iddan co-founded it in 1998 with others

Swain: working prototypes were produced in January 1999 by the Given Imaging R&D group, headed by Dr. Arkady Glukhovsky

disagreements.question: Where was the first capsule swallowed?

claims.quote: All the other technologies combined could find the source of the problem in only 40% of the patients.

claims.text: לדברי פרופ' אורי קופילוב משיבא, הגלולה רגישה יותר ממדידת MRI בזיהוי ממצאים דלקתיים בקרוהן.
claims.quote: הגלולה רגישה יותר בזיהוי ממצאים דלקתיים בהשוואה לבדיקת MRI, ומאפשרת גילוי מחלה בשלב מוקדם יותר מעבר לאבחון.

claims.text: לדברי ד"ר לורנס קסלברנר, הגלולה מצילת חיים כי בלעדיה רבים לא היו עושים קולונוסקופיה.
claims.quote: הגלולה הזו מצילת חיים כי בלעדיה, הרבה מאוד אנשים לא היו עושים בדיקות קולונוסקופיה

claims.text: לפי כותב הסקירה, אידן סיפר לו שרופא אמר לו שבזכות הקפסולה הצליח להציל חיי מטופל.
claims.quote: Because of your capsule, I was able to save a patient’s life! Iddan had realized his dream.

claims.text: ביולי נתן ה-FDA לחברה אישור למכור את הקפסולה כאבחון קו ראשון בבעיות של המעי הדק.
claims.quote: In July, the Food and Drug Administration gave the firm permission to sell the camera-pill as a first-line diagnosis in the evaluation of small intestine problems.

claims.text: לפי Forward, החברה מתכננת לפתח את הקפסולה לאבחון בעיות בקיבה ובושט.
claims.quote: Given plans to develop the capsule to diagnose problems in the stomach and in the esophagus

claims.text: עד יוני כ-600 בתי חולים ומרפאות בארצות הברית הציעו את טכנולוגיית הקפסולה למטופלים.
claims.quote: As of June, some 600 hospitals and medical offices in the United States offered the capsule technology to patients.

claims.text: כ-32,000 אמריקאים בלעו את הקפסולה, יחד עם 20,000 נוספים בשאר העולם.
claims.quote: Some 32,000 Americans have gulped down the camera-pill, along with another 20,000 people in the rest of the world.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Link, כיום מבוצעות בעולם יותר משני מיליון בדיקות קפסולה בשנה.
claims.quote: At this time, over 2 million capsule endoscopies are performed annually worldwide.

claims.text: החברה נרכשה על ידי מדטרוניק, שהשאירה את הפיתוח והייצור בישראל.
claims.quote: נרכשה לאחר מספר שנים על ידי תאגיד מדטרוניק העולמי וזו בצעד חסר תקדים השאירה את הפיתוח והייצור בישראל

claims.text: לפי ynet, הפילקאם היא גאווה ישראלית שנבלעת כיום על ידי מיליוני בני אדם בעולם.
claims.quote: גלולת הפילקאם היא גאווה ישראלית, שנכנסה לרשימת ההמצאות הישראליות של כל הזמנים, נבלעת כיום על ידי מיליוני בני אדם ברחבי העולם

claims.text: לפי הרופאים, המכשיר אינו יכול לטפל בבעיות שהוא מוצא.
claims.quote: But the device cannot treat the problems it finds, doctors point out

claims.text: לקפסולה אין כלים כירורגיים כמו באנדוסקופ קונבנציונלי לביופסיות, לטיפול בדימום או להסרת פוליפים.
claims.quote: Nor is the capsule fitted with surgical tools like a conventional endoscope to take biopsies, treat bleeding lesions or remove polyps.

claims.text: חוקרים אחרים אמרו שהקפסולה, לפחות בצורתה הנוכחית, מוגבלת מכדי להחליף אנדוסקופים.
claims.quote: But they said the capsule, at least in its current form, is too limited to replace endoscopes

claims.text: החיסרון העיקרי של PillCam וממשיכיה הוא היעדר שליטה בתנועה.
claims.quote: The main drawback of the PillCam and its successors is the lack of control of movement

claims.text: העלות הגבוהה יחסית של ההתקנים החד-פעמיים מנעה מהם להתעלות על אנדוסקופיה קונבנציונלית.
claims.quote: the relatively high cost of the disposable devices have prevented them from overtaking conventional endoscopy

claims.text: לפי Forward, בכ-1% מהמטופלים הקפסולה עלולה להיתקע בהיצרות או בחסימה במעי הדק.
claims.quote: the capsule might get stuck at a stricture or an obstruction in the small intestine

claims.text: לפי Jewish Link, אחת לכ-1,000 בדיקות הקפסולה נתקעת וצריך לאחזר אותה.
claims.quote: Once in about 1,000 procedures the capsule gets stuck and has to be retrieved in some fashion.

claims.text: ד"ר גבי עידן פגש את שכנו, הגסטרואנטרולוג פרופ' איתן סקפה, ששיתף אותו בקושי לבצע אנדוסקופיה במעי הדק.
claims.quote: את שכנו הגסטרואנטרולוג פרופ' איתן סקפה, שסיפר לו על הקושי לבצע אנדוסקופיה במעי הדק

claims.text: לפי המאמר, שכנו של אידן פיתח מחלה בקיבה ואידן הבין שאין טכנולוגיה לבדיקת המעי הדק.
claims.quote: His neighbor, Dr. Scappa, developed some type of stomach ailment and Iddan became aware that there was no technology available

claims.text: לפי Forward, ד"ר גבריאל אידן הוא מהנדס מכונות שעבד על התקני הדמיה ברפאל, חברת מחקר ופיתוח ישראלית בבעלות ממשלתית.
claims.quote: Dr. Gavriel J. Iddan is a mechanical engineer who worked on imaging devices for Rafael, an Israeli government-owned research and development company

claims.text: לפי סקירה ב-PMC, הפטנט המקורי של אידן ניתן ב-1997 ותיאר שבב CCD שהיה גדול מדי וצרך יותר מדי אנרגיה.
claims.quote: The original patent of Gavriel Iddan (awarded in 1997) envisioned a CCD chip, which was too bulky and consumed too much energy.

claims.text: לפי Jewish Link, הפטנט על הקפסולה ניתן ב-1999 במסגרת Given Imaging.
claims.quote: Ultimately the device, capsule endoscopy, was created under the aegis of a new biotechnology company, Given Imaging, with a patent in 1999.

claims.text: לפי סוויין, אבות טיפוס עובדים הופקו בינואר 1999 על ידי קבוצת המו"פ של Given Imaging בראשות ד"ר ארקדי גלוחובסקי.
claims.quote: working prototypes were produced in January 1999 by the Given Imaging R&D group headed by Dr. Arkady Glukhovsky

claims.text: לפי ynet, פרופ' סקפה ביצע את הניסויים הקליניים הראשונים בבני אדם, והגלולה הראשונה נבלעה במרפאתו הפרטית ברמת השרון.
claims.quote: פרופ' סקפה ביצע את הניסויים הקליניים הראשונים בבני אדם והגלולה הראשונה נבלעה במרפאה הפרטית שלו ברמת השרון

claims.text: לפי Forward, במשך שמונה שעות המצלמה מצלמת שתי תמונות בשנייה.
claims.quote: For eight hours, the camera takes internal pictures at a rate of two frames per second

claims.text: גבריאל אידן, מהנדס ישראלי שעבד ברפאל, הוא הממציא של האנדוסקופיה האלחוטית בקפסולה.
claims.quote: Israeli inventor Gavriel Iddan's development of a pill-sized camera for wireless capsule endoscopy

claims.text: גבריאל אידן, מהנדס ישראלי שעבד ברפאל, הוא הממציא של האנדוסקופיה האלחוטית בקפסולה.
claims.quote: Iddan took a sabbatical from his regular position as a senior engineer at the electro optical design section of Rafael

claims.text: הכרה: מועמד לפרס הממציא האירופי, 2011
claims.quote: US, Israeli and Indian scientists behind turbines for power generation in shallow or sluggish water, miniscule camera technology for endoscopy and an ultraviolet technique for water disinfectant are also nominated under a non-European section.

claims.text: אידן ראה שאפשר למזער טכנולוגיית טילים למוצר רפואי.
claims.quote: Iddan had worked on the seeker, or the “eye” of the missile, which captures the targets and guides it

claims.text: ב-PillCam SB אין צורך בהרדמה.
claims.quote: The procedure requires no bowel preparation or sedation.

claims.text: ב-8 בדצמבר 2013 הודיעה קוביידיין על הסכם לרכוש את Given Imaging ב-30 דולר למניה במזומן.
claims.quote: Covidien will acquire all of the outstanding shares of Given Imaging for $30.00 per share in cash.

claims.text: מהנדס אלקטרו-אופטי
claims.quote: Gavriel Iddan, born in Haifa in 1941, was an electro-optical engineer (whatever that is)

claims.text: אידן יצר אב טיפוס ב-1998, אחרי כמעט עשרים שנות עבודה על הרעיון
claims.quote: By 1998, he had developed a prototype for an ingestible wireless capsule

claims.text: אידן יצר אב טיפוס ב-1998, אחרי כמעט עשרים שנות עבודה על הרעיון
claims.quote: This began his 20-year quest to solve the problem.

claims.text: אין צורך בהרדמה, אבל צריך הכנת מעיים
claims.quote: without sedation or gas insufflation

claims.text: אין צורך בהרדמה, אבל צריך הכנת מעיים
claims.quote: laxative bowel preparation is crucial

quote_translations.c62: In 2001, the PillCam pill was approved for use in Israel, in the United States and later also in Europe.
quote_translations.c83: After the meeting he began developing a pill equipped with a video camera, which would allow doctors to diagnose diseases and bleeding
quote_translations.c60: I began my experiments together with friends from Rafael. I found myself testing the concept of the development on a frozen chicken I had bought at the supermarket
quote_translations.c64: The pill is more sensitive in detecting inflammatory findings compared with an MRI examination, and enables detection of disease at an earlier stage beyond diagnosis.
quote_translations.c82: This pill is life-saving because without it, a great many people would not undergo colonoscopy examinations
quote_translations.c63: was acquired several years later by the global corporation Medtronic, which in an unprecedented step kept development and manufacturing in Israel
quote_translations.c65: The PillCam pill is an Israeli source of pride, which entered the list of Israeli inventions of all time, and is swallowed today by millions of people around the world
quote_translations.c59: his neighbor, the gastroenterologist Prof. Eitan Scapa, who told him about the difficulty of performing endoscopy in the small intestine
quote_translations.c61: Prof. Scapa conducted the first clinical trials in humans, and the first pill was swallowed at his private clinic in Ramat HaSharon
